newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S. Marines arrive in Kuwait for exercise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Marines arrive in Kuwait for exercise.

text.p: Some 2,200 U.S. Marines began landing in Kuwait on Friday to hold manoeuvres with the Gulf Arab state's troops.
"We are supposed to establish...security and stability in this region," Marine Captain Scott Lopez, a spokesman for the 11th Marine Expditionary Unit, told reporters.
The Marines, landing by helicopter and hovercraft from their ships, will train with Kuwaiti forces under exercise Eager Mace-97 that runs until the end of January, he said.
"The fact that we are here over our national holidays is indicative of how important this is to our national policy," said Lopez of Santa Fe, New Mexico.
Three ships -- USS Cleveland, USS Harpersferry and USS Essex -- carried the troops, based in Camp Pendleton, California, and their equipment to Kuwait for the scheduled exercise, he said.

About three-quarters of the troops were to land on Friday and the rest in the next two days. The troops are basing at Camp Doha north of Kuwait City and the Adera Range, some 40 km (25 miles) south of the Iraqi border.
The force has six AV-8B Harrier aircraft that will take part in enforcing a 1992 Western-imposed no-fly zone in Iraq, he said.
Some 4,200 U.S. soldiers deployed in Kuwait in Washington's September standoff with Baghdad finished their pullout earlier this month, a U.S. official said.

A U.S.-led coalition drove Iraqi troops from Kuwait in 1991. Since then the United States has kept weapons, including main battle tanks, in Kuwait to be used by U.S. troops to deter any Iraqi threat. Washington also keeps eight stealth fighters in Kuwait.
